# Chapter 7: Regulation of Metabolic Flux

## 7.3 Feedback Inhibition

Feedback inhibition is defined as the reduction of an enzyme's activity by the accumulation of a downstream pathway product.

**Definition:** Allosteric feedback inhibition refers to binding of the end product at a regulatory site distinct from the active site.

In many amino acid biosynthesis pathways, the end-product inhibits the first committed enzyme of the pathway when its concentration rises. This mechanism prevents wasteful overproduction of the amino acid under normal growth conditions.

Figure 7.4: Schematic of end-product feedback inhibition on the first committed step of a linear biosynthetic pathway, showing the product binding the regulatory site of enzyme E1.

## 7.5 Metabolic Burden

Metabolic burden is defined as the fitness cost imposed on a host cell by heterologous protein expression or pathway flux.

High-level expression of a heterologous pathway causes metabolic burden, which reduces host growth rate and can lower overall productivity.
